newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles Myer says first qtr sales rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles Myer says first qtr sales rise.

text.p: Coles Myer Ltd said sales for the 13 weeks to October 27 rose 5.6 per cent to A$4.445 billion from A$4.211 billion a year ago.
Managing director Peter Bartels said the sales growth was satisfactory and in line with the company's budgets.
Coles Myer said the sales increase was well ahead of inflation, but lower than the rate of recent quarters.
This was a reflection of the general slowing in retail sales across the country.
Coles said supermarket and liquor sales rose 11.0 per cent, and market share continued to grow.
Myer Grace Bros sales rose nearly 2.0 per cent, excluding the Grace Bros Sydney store which is being redeveloped and trading in only 30 per cent of its floorspace.
Including the Sydney store, sales were 0.8 per cent below last year.

First quarter sales at Kmart were 5.3 percent below last year. This was in line with the revised business strategy and good progress was being made in improving underlying core sales and margins, Coles said.
Apparel group sales rose 4.8 percent, including a 9.3 percent increase from Target.
Target's result included a positive trend in comparable store sales. Katies sales were below last year after a slow start to the spring/summer season in ladies apparel, it said.
Chief operating officer business units Dennis Eck said the supermarkets and liquor businesses, together with Target and Officeworks, continued to exceed growth in their market segments.
The department stores were matching the performance of their major competitors, but Kmart and Katies were performing below their market average.
Bartels said Coles had adopted a cautious approach to the critical Christmas period.
"But we are hopeful that customers will respond positively to the stable economic environment and adopt a more relaxed approach to spending over the next few months," he said.
